_comment: How the rival realms play. Every number here is [GEN] and meant to be retuned by hand - the AI reads this file and has no constants of its own. See docs/MECHANICS.md section 8.
_difficulties: One setting, chosen at the start, applied to every rival at once. KNIGHT IS THE HONEST RUNG: incomePermille 1000 means no handicap and no assistance, exactly the player's rules. Below it the AI is crippled, above it it is subsidised - and the subsidy is stated openly rather than hidden.

difficulties.name: Recruit
difficulties.blurb: Poor, timid and easily distracted. It will build a realm and mostly leave you alone.

difficulties.name: Squire
difficulties.blurb: Slightly behind you, and slow to commit. It expands into open ground but rarely picks a fight.

difficulties.name: Knight
difficulties.blurb: Your equal. No bonus, no penalty - the same economy and the same rules you play by.

difficulties.name: Baron
difficulties.blurb: Richer than you, and it presses an advantage. It relieves its own sieges and takes fair fights.

difficulties.name: King
difficulties.blurb: Half again your income, never wastes a month, and will attack on even numbers.

_personalities: Per realm, and fixed for the campaign. build weights are relative - the highest-scoring affordable option wins, so doubling a weight roughly doubles how often that line gets chosen. aggressionPermille MULTIPLIES the difficulty's odds requirement, so 700 means it attacks at 0.7x the odds its difficulty would otherwise demand and 2200 means it wants more than twice as much. bullyFloorPermille is the least a rival realm may be worth, relative to this one, before it is beneath attacking.

personalities.name: Ambitious
personalities.blurb: Leans outward. Expands hardest, ranges a little further from home and keeps the smallest garrison.

personalities.name: Defensive
personalities.blurb: Leans inward. Builds walls first, holds an extra unit in every settlement and consolidates its own ground before it looks past it.

personalities.name: Balanced
personalities.blurb: The centre the other four lean off. Builds an economy, keeps an army, and takes ground when the odds are good.

personalities.name: Peaceful
personalities.blurb: Economy first. It builds and settles harder than anyone and keeps a smaller army — but it still recruits, still expands, and still makes war when the odds are good.

personalities.name: Honorable
personalities.blurb: Plays exactly as Balanced does today. Honour is a matter of who it will deal with, not how it fights, so the difference lands with diplomacy.
